title: Tea Mosquito bug in Guava and Avocado

Header: Tea Mosquito bug in Guava and Avocado
Helopeltis antonii Sinhala - Capsid Makuna; Tamil – Nulambu Mooddu Poochchi

Prevention: Prune to expose the trees for proper sun light inside the canopy
Avoid application of broad spectrum insecticide to conserve natural enemies
Practise bagging of fruits at early stage
Control weeds to destroy alternative hosts
Monitoring: Detect reddish brown adult bugs (6.5 - 8.5mm long) and nymphs in early morning / late evening by using hand nets
Look for following symptoms – feeding punctures and discoloured necrotic lesions on shoots and leaves (in

Thrips damage entire fruit surface brown with an alligator skin appearance and elongate feeding scars.) corky growth appearance or scab on fruits brown centred black lesions especially near to the main veins of leaves
Direct Control: Prune and destroy heavily infested plant parts
Collect and destroy adults and nymphs using a sweep net
Apply neem seed kernel extract (50g seeds/ lit. of water)
Rate of dilution - 10ml / 10 lit. of water
Restrictions: Apply only to foliage and avoid during fruiting stage.
Toxic to bees and natural enemies.
